Phased Antenna Array

An antenna array built from an EM result: one element, a small sub-array, or the whole array solved once. In Elements mode it has one pin per element, Rows × Cols of them, numbered row-major from the top left as seen from boresight, and each pin is that element's port: wire a source, an amplifier or a feed network to it. Its pitch dx, dy is a length in any unit, or an expression such as 0.5*lambda(f0). A type=fields analysis naming it gives the whole array's pattern.

With Mode=feed it has one pin, F, and the beamformer inside: the feed is split N ways and element n is driven through its weight Amp·e^(jφ) (and a delay Delay), rounded to PhaseBits and AttenStep, then through its own copy of the cell Channel names, if any (its first port in, its second out, placed as PA1.ch[n]). Amp, Phase and Delay are evaluated once per element with n, row, col, x and y bound, so Phase=steer(theta0,0,f0) steers the beam and Amp=taylor(-30,4) tapers it; Phase[n] sets one element's phase. Feed mode takes up to 4096 elements, and a sweep of the steering VAR is an ordinary parametric sweep. BeamNfDb(F1) on the fields analysis is the noise figure from the driving port to the beam's peak.

As a receiver, the elements' noise is what their patterns see: Tsky is the brightness above the horizon, in kelvin, a temperature or an expression of the elevation el (5+280*exp(-el/(5*pi/180))), and Tground the brightness below it where the record's pattern reaches there (a planar record's ground plane hides it). Left blank, both are the array's own temperature, which is the noise any passive block has. A plane wave arriving at the array is RxTheta[k], RxPhi[k] (degrees), RxPd[k] (its power density, dBm/m²), RxFreq[k] and RxPol[k] (theta, phi, rhcp, lhcp or an angle from θ̂ towards φ̂): each element receives it through its own pattern, and in harmonic balance and envelope runs it is a tone like a 1-Tone source's, so a signal and an interferer pass through the channels together. An interferer reaches each channel through the element's pattern and is only beamformed after it. With a fields analysis F1 driven from the receive port and an S-parameter analysis NF1 with Noise=yes, AntennaTempK(F1), SystemTempK(F1, NF1), GoverTDbK(F1, NF1) (dB/K), SnrDb(F1, NF1, k, bandwidth) for wave k and NullDepthDb(F1, theta, phi) read the receive side; all of them work through amplifiers that only pass signal one way.

The symbol draws the aperture as seen from the front: a square per element up to 8 × 8 (a larger array shows its top-left 8 × 8 and its size), a triangular lattice's rows offset, an element switched off hollow. In Feed mode a beam leaves its right side, tilted by θ0 with θ0 30° φ0 0° written beside it when Phase (or Delay) is a steer(); in Elements mode its four corner elements are numbered and hovering on a pin names its element, row, column and position. Values written as VARs are read from the schematic's VAR blocks.

Couplingon——on, or off: off keeps each element's own reflection and drops every coupling between elements.
Off———Elements switched off, as a list of element numbers (3,17): each is terminated in Z0 — in Elements mode inside, its pin left open; in Feed mode by its zero weight.
Amp———Feed mode: each element's amplitude, linear, evaluated once per element with n, row, col, x and y bound (taylor(-30,4), chebyshev(-30), cosq(1)). Amp[n] sets one element's. Blank is 1.
Phase—deg—Feed mode: each element's phase, degrees, evaluated per element as Amp is: steer(theta0, phi0, f0) points the beam. Phase[n] sets one element's. Blank is 0.
Delay—ns—Feed mode: each element's true time delay, evaluated per element as Amp is: steerDelay(theta0, phi0) points the beam at every frequency. Delay[n] sets one element's. Blank is 0.
PhaseBits———Feed mode: each phase is rounded to 360°/2^PhaseBits. 0 or blank is continuous.
AttenStep—dB—Feed mode: each amplitude's attenuation from the largest is rounded to this step, in dB. 0 or blank is continuous.
Channel———Feed mode: a two-port cell placed once per element between its weight and the element (its first port in, its second out), as PA1.ch[n]. Its expressions may read n, row, col, x and y. Blank connects each weight to its element directly.
Z0—Ω—Reference impedance at the elements. Blank takes the record's.
Tsky———The brightness above the horizon, kelvin: a temperature, or an expression of the elevation el (5+280*exp(-el/(5*pi/180))). The elements' noise is what their patterns see of it. Blank is the array's own temperature, the noise a passive block has.
Tground———The brightness below the horizon, kelvin, where the record's pattern reaches there (a planar record has a ground plane and does not). Blank is the array's own temperature.
RecordRows———The lattice of a record that does not store its ports' positions, its ports numbered row-major. Ignored when it does.
RecordCols———The lattice of a record that does not store its ports' positions, its ports numbered row-major. Ignored when it does.
RecordDx—mm—The lattice of a record that does not store its ports' positions, its ports numbered row-major. Ignored when it does.
RecordDy—mm—The lattice of a record that does not store its ports' positions, its ports numbered row-major. Ignored when it does.

Annotation components

Propagation Channel

Everything between a transmit antenna's terminals and a receive antenna's terminals that is not an antenna: path loss, multipath and Doppler. Pin tx is the transmit antenna and pin rx the receive antenna, each over ground, and they are not interchangeable. The channel is one way: it carries what arrives at tx to rx and sends nothing back, so its S12 is 0. A reverse link is a second channel, and Reverse=CH1 makes it the same path with its ends exchanged.

PropagationChannel:CH1 tx rx Distance=250 TxHeight=10 RxHeight=1.5 PathLoss=tworay TxGain=8 RxGain=0
  • Ends. TxGain and RxGain are antenna gains in dBi, the same in every direction. TxPattern or RxPattern names one port of an EM result's far field instead, written path#port: that end then has the port's realized gain toward each ray and the port's S11 as its impedance, and its boresight points at the other end unless TxAz/TxEl/TxRoll say otherwise. TxZ and RxZ are the impedances the pins present (default 50 Ω). The receive pin's noise is its impedance at the antenna temperature RxTant, which defaults to the ambient temperature. The channel adds no noise of its own.
  • Geometry. Distance is the horizontal distance between the ends in metres, at heights TxHeight and RxHeight. Write a bare number or metre: m means milli in every value, so Distance=150 m is refused rather than read as 15 cm. TxPos and RxPos place both ends as x,y,z instead. TxVel and RxVel, as x,y,z in m/s, give each ray its Doppler.
  • Large scale. PathLoss is any model of the propagation library (free, logdist, multislope, tworay, 38901, P1238, P1411, P526, satellite, P1812). Its parameters, and the added losses (gas, rain, clutter and the rest), are written beside it by the model's own names. A placed channel shows a dozen of its parameters; + in its Parameter dialog adds any other by name, with what it does. Rain=fixed adds the attenuation at the stated availability.
  • Drops. Each channel is one drop, numbered by Drop under Seed. A drop draws the shadowing from the model's σ (in dB, added to the loss; Shadowing=off holds it at 0). It also draws the line-of-sight state from the model's probability when Los=auto, and with Rain=drawn a time percentage, taking the rain exceeded for it. That rain is zero beyond P.530's 1 % or P.618's 5 %. Every draw depends only on Seed, Drop and the channel's name, so drop 37 alone equals drop 37 in a sweep. The run reports link:CH1:Shadowing_dB, LosState (1, 0, or NaN when not drawn) and RainTime_pct.
  • Scenario drops. Multipath=scenario with PathLoss=38901 draws a TR 38.901 drop for the ends' geometry, with the transmit end as the base station. Each drop draws the scenario's correlated large-scale parameters (shadowing, K, delay and angle spreads), then its clusters' delays, powers and angles, 20 rays a cluster, their cross-polar ratios and phases. The run reports them as DS_s, ASD_deg, ASA_deg, ZSD_deg, ZSA_deg and K_dB. The spreads, K and Doppler come from the scenario, so DelaySpread, KFactor, the angle spreads, Fading, Velocity and fD don't apply to it.
  • Satellite states. States=p681 on PathLoss=satellite applies ITU-R P.681's land mobile-satellite model. The link moves between a GOOD state (line of sight and light shadowing) and a BAD state (heavy shadowing and blockage). Each state has lognormal event lengths and its own Loo statistics: a lognormal direct signal plus Rayleigh multipath. The parameter set is the one for StateEnvironment nearest the frequency and elevation, valid from 1.5 to 20 GHz above 20°. The terminal moves at Velocity (m/s); still, the drop is one state. The run reports State (1 GOOD, 0 BAD) and, in an envelope run, StateGood_frac. P.681's current edition has two states, not three.
  • Monte Carlo. A sweep over Drop is the Monte Carlo: Drop=drop on the channel, a variable drop, and analysis MC type=parametric_sweep Var=drop Start=1 Stop=500 Step=1 Inner=ENV1. outage_over(x, threshold, "drop") gives the fraction of drops below a threshold, with its 95 % interval as lo and hi. cdf, pctl_over, mean_over, std_over and yield_over work over the same axis. In an envelope sweep, a transmit side that is the same in every drop is solved once. Each later drop solves only its receive side, driven by the recorded transmit waves, and the result is the same as solving both. A transmit array whose beam the channel picks per drop is solved once per distinct beam. The run says how many drops reused it. A DC supply shared by both sides prevents this. The receive side is still solved in every drop. A receive array whose channel cells are identical and linear is replaced by its feed for the run: the reflection the closed array presents, with the rays arriving there, so a drop of a 1 µs record into 4096 elements takes seconds. The run says so; a run with Noise=yes keeps the array, whose cells' noise is part of it. Nonlinear cells are solved element by element: about 4 s a drop at 64 elements and a minute at 256, so a Monte Carlo over many drops into 1024 or more nonlinear elements is impractical.
  • Rays. Multipath=none uses the rays of the geometry: the line of sight, plus the ground ray for tworay. Multipath=tdl uses a tapped delay line named by Profile=. Multipath=file reads taps from File=, a CSV whose header names delay (ns), power (dB), and optionally phase (deg), doppler (Hz), k (dB) and spectrum. A sampled impulse response writes re and im in place of power and phase. Each row is one tap, with its delay in excess of the line of sight. A file whose powers don't sum to 1 is normalized, and the run says by how much: the large-scale loss carries the mean power.
  • Tapped delay lines. Profile= is one of TR 38.901's TDL-A to TDL-E, TS 36.104's EPA, EVA and ETU, ITU-R M.1225's PedA, PedB, VehA and VehB, or TR 38.811's NTN-TDL-A to NTN-TDL-D. Each table is embedded with its document's edition. The TDL and NTN-TDL delays are normalized, so DelaySpread (in seconds) is required for them and their delays are scaled until the RMS delay spread equals it exactly. The tables in ns are used as printed unless DelaySpread is stated. TDL-D, TDL-E, NTN-TDL-C and NTN-TDL-D have a line-of-sight tap, and KFactor (dB) rescales them as TR 38.901 §7.7.6 describes. A terrain profile for P526 or P1812 is written Terrain=.
  • Array ends. Tx=PA1 or Rx=PA1 names a Phased Antenna Array (either mode). That end is the array's own elements: their patterns, their positions, and an orientation from TxAz/TxEl/TxRoll (or Rx…), facing the other end when unstated. Such an end has no pin, so the symbol draws only the pins that remain, and the two kinds mix (a pin source into an array, an array into a pin, or array to array). The coupling is stamped as two unknowns per ray, never as a matrix of receive elements by transmit elements, and a receive element takes exactly the wave PAA-7's incident wave from that direction gives it. Several channels may end on one array; their waves add on its elements. check and the run warn when the ends are closer than 2D²/λ for an array's aperture D. An EM Field Data block may be an end too, each port radiating and receiving through its record's pattern, in S-parameter and harmonic-balance runs (an envelope run refuses it for now).
  • Receive arrays on the fast path. A Feed-mode receive array whose channel cells are identical and linear (the conditions the Phased Array's fast path states) takes each channel's rays as one source at its feed instead of on every element. The result is the same, and the run says whether this happened and why. A harmonic-balance run then reports link:CH1:FeedPower_dBm, the power that channel alone delivers at the feed into a matched load. For an array several channels reach, it also reports link:PA1:SIR_dB[channel], each one's power over the sum of the others'. The array's own noise at the feed comes from the S-parameter noise analysis (SystemTempK).
  • Clustered delay lines and ray lists. Multipath=cdl with Profile= one of TR 38.901's CDL-A to CDL-E or TR 38.811's NTN-CDL-A to NTN-CDL-D gives rays with directions and polarization. Their delays are scaled to DelaySpread, the angle spreads to ASD, ASA, ZSD and ZSA (degrees) when stated, and the clusters are turned so the line-of-sight cluster lies on the line between the ends. Multipath=rays reads a ray list from File= with delay (ns), power (dB), theta_d (deg), phi_d (deg), theta_a (deg), phi_a (deg), and optionally xpr (dB) or a 2×2 matrix (tt_re, tt_im, … pp_im). The angles are in the global frame, or in each end's own frame with RayFrame=ends. Each such ray's Doppler comes from TxVel, RxVel and its own directions.
  • Beam. When an end is a Feed-mode array whose Phase is a steer(), the run picks its beam through this channel. Each end's candidates are a grid in (u, v), one beamwidth apart, reaching out to ScanLimit (60° by default). Each candidate goes through the array's own steer() and PhaseBits, or Codebook= names a CSV of theta, phi in degrees (a third column tx, rx or both picks the end). Every pair of candidates is scored by the power the array factors and the centre element's pattern carry through the drop's rays at TimeOffset, averaged across the signal's band in an envelope run. BeamSearch=exhaustive scores every pair; alternating, the default past a million pairs, fixes one end and picks the other's best, then the reverse. BeamSelect=auto (the default) takes the strongest pair. rank with BeamRank=n takes the n-th strongest distinct pair: a pair within one beamwidth of a stronger one at both ends is the same path and isn't counted. index with TxBeam=/RxBeam= takes a codebook entry (a number from 1) or a direction (θ, φ). manual keeps the arrays' own weights. The beam is set for the run only, without elaborating again: the schematic keeps its steer(). auto, rank or index written on an array whose weights aren't a steer() is refused. Left blank on such an array, the weights are used as written. The run reports link:CH1:Beam_dB[pair], BeamRank[pair], BeamTx[pair] and BeamRx[pair] (the two codebook entries) for every pair scored, strongest first, the codebooks as TxCodebook_deg and RxCodebook_deg, and BeamChosen, TxBeam_deg and RxBeam_deg. It also reports BeamBound_dB, the best any phase-only weights could do through these rays, and BeamCodebookLoss_dB, the chosen pair's shortfall against it. explain --analysis lists the same. In the Phased Array tool, the Channel tab of an array that is a channel end draws the drop's rays and the candidates on the (u, v) map and lists the ranked pairs. A click on a pair or a ray selects it (BeamSelect=index). Apply writes the directions into the arrays' steer() and sets BeamSelect=manual. Each is one undo step, and the drop slider only shows another realization.
  • Polarization. Each ray carries its 2×2 polarization matrix (the line of sight's is diag(1, −1)). A gain end's polarization is TxPol/RxPol (theta, phi, rhcp, lhcp or an angle) in its own frame, or matched to the other end along the line of sight when unstated. Faraday= (degrees) rotates every ray's field. On a satellite path with Ionosphere=on, P.531's rotation is applied this way whenever an end has a polarization, and its polarization-loss term is then dropped.
  • Fading. Fading=rayleigh, rician (with KFactor, a line-of-sight component at 0.7 f_D and its own phase) or nakagami (with NakagamiM) makes each tap's gain fade. Left blank, a profile's taps fade as the profile says, and none or a plain file stays static. Doppler=classical, flat, gaussian or los is the Doppler spectrum. The maximum Doppler is fD, or Velocity (m/s) times the carrier over c, or the ends' relative speed from TxVel and RxVel. Each tap is a sum of Sinusoids sinusoids (64 by default). Every draw comes from Seed and Drop, so drop 37 run alone is the same as drop 37 inside a sweep over Drop, and adding a tap leaves the other taps unchanged.

What each analysis sees:

Analysis The channel
S-parameter, noise A two-port frozen at TimeOffset: S21 = H(f), S12 = 0, S11 and S22 the ends' impedances
Harmonic balance The same frozen H at every tone, each at its own frequency, with no Doppler shift and the fading frozen
Envelope Every ray's delayed transmit wave, rotated, scaled, faded and turned by its Doppler, drives the receive pin

H(f) is λ/(4πd) times the model's loss in excess of free space, times each ray's gain, delay and antenna gains, summed over the rays. d is the distance the model uses (the slant range on a satellite path). The excess loss is the model's at f0: the stated f0, otherwise the run's carrier, otherwise each frequency asked. The free-space part follows λ at every frequency. The bulk delay d/c (3.3 µs at 1 km) is reported and never simulated. In an envelope run the channel adds one step of latency plus each ray's excess delay, reads only steps already solved, and leaves the receive side's first latency out of every measurement. A cycle of channels in an envelope bench is refused, and so is a receive pin driven by two channels.

Each run adds the loss breakdown, the total path loss, the bulk delay, the common Doppler and the rays to its result, as link:CH1:Loss_dB, link:CH1:PathLoss_dB, Delay0_s, Doppler0_Hz and its rate Drift0_Hzps (a satellite pass's), and the rest; link:CH1:Gain_dB, the drop's 20·log10|H| at the reference frequency with the antenna gains, shadowing and fading in it; and, with Rain, link:CH1:Rain_dB, the rain term alone. A measurement reads any of them as SP1.link("CH1", "Gain_dB"), over every sweep axis of the run. It also adds the small scale: RmsDelaySpread_s, CoherenceBandwidth_Hz, fD_Hz, the coherence time Tc_s (where the correlation first falls to one half, 0.24/f_D for the classical spectrum), PowerDelayProfile_dB, the drop's DopplerSpectrum_dB, and TapGain over the record. An envelope run adds H across the signal's band over the record, fDxTrecord and fDoverSCS, and the Signal quality preset then draws the power-delay profile and the Doppler spectrum under its table. With Equalizer=genie the equalizer divides by the channel's own H(f, t), fading included, so what remains is the inter-carrier interference the fading causes within each symbol. explain --analysis states the same, with the envelope regime: the Doppler spread and coherence time against the record and the subcarrier spacing, and the coherence bandwidth against the signal's.

NetTerminal
1tx
2rx

The nets of an instance line, in this order. How many there are is set by Tx and Rx; the table shows Tx and Rx = 2. tx is the transmit antenna's terminals and rx the receive antenna's, each over ground. NOT interchangeable: the channel carries tx to rx and nothing back, so a reverse link is a second channel (Reverse= for the same realization).

NameDefaultUnitOn schematicMeaning
Distance100metreshownHorizontal distance between the two antennas, metres (a bare number; m alone is milli). The ends are at heights TxHeight and RxHeight above a flat ground.
TxHeight1.5metre—Transmit antenna height above the ground, metres.
RxHeight1.5metre—Receive antenna height above the ground, metres.
PathLossfree—shownThe large-scale model, by its recommendation or report (free, logdist, multislope, tworay, 38901, P1238, P1411, P526, satellite, P1812). Its parameters, and the added losses, are written beside it by the model's own names.
Multipathnone——none: the rays the geometry gives (the line of sight, and tworay's ground ray). tdl: a tapped delay line by Profile=. cdl: a clustered delay line by Profile= (rays with directions and polarization). file: the taps of a power-delay profile (File=). rays: a ray list with departure and arrival directions (File=). scenario: a TR 38.901 drop for the 38901 model's scenario (its spreads, clusters and rays drawn per drop).
Tx——shownA Phased Antenna Array's instance name: that end is the array's own elements (their patterns, positions and orientation from Az/El/Roll) and has no pin. Blank: the end is a pin.
Rx——shownA Phased Antenna Array's instance name: that end is the array's own elements (their patterns, positions and orientation from Az/El/Roll) and has no pin. Blank: the end is a pin.
TxGain0——Transmit antenna gain, dBi, the same in every direction. TxPattern replaces it with a pattern.
RxGain0——Receive antenna gain, dBi, the same in every direction. RxPattern replaces it with a pattern.
TxZ50Ω—The impedance the transmit pin presents, ohms.
RxZ50Ω—The impedance of the source the receive pin is, ohms.
TimeOffset0s—The instant, seconds, an S-parameter or harmonic-balance run freezes the channel at (Doppler phases turn with time); where an envelope run's time 0 is.

Variables (VAR)

A port-less annotation holding name = expression variable definitions, scoped to where it is placed — global at the test bench top, or local inside a cell. Variables are sweepable. Edit the rows in the multi-line text editor by double-clicking the VAR. No fixed parameters.

Measurements (MEAS)

A port-less annotation holding name = expression measurement equations, evaluated after a run — for example Pout_dBm = 10*log10(...). Measurements attach at the top test-bench level only. Edit the rows in the same multi-line editor as VAR. No fixed parameters.

How to write one: Measurements covers reading an analysis's results (nodes, probes, harmonics, sweeps and frequency), and Expressions covers the language itself: operators, functions and units. The editor's Help button opens the first of these.
